GRIEVANCE V ◆ CONSTITUTIONAL RESTRAINT

He has permitted removal of residents without the hearing and process that the Constitution requires.

THE RECORD SHOWS

The administration acknowledged deporting Kilmar Abrego Garcia in error, while the Supreme Court required it to facilitate his release and due process challenges continued.

A federal filing acknowledged that Abrego Garcia was sent to El Salvador despite an order protecting him from removal there. The Supreme Court directed the government to facilitate his release from Salvadoran custody, while separately requiring notice and an opportunity to challenge removals under the Alien Enemies Act. The administration says it is enforcing immigration law and disputes some allegations about individual detainees. This entry concerns legal procedure and compliance, not a general claim that noncitizens cannot be deported.

A DOCUMENTED SEQUENCE

3 MILESTONES
  1. March 2025The government sent Kilmar Abrego Garcia to El Salvador despite a protective removal order.
  2. April 10, 2025The Supreme Court required the government to facilitate his release from Salvadoran custody.
  3. April–May 2025Federal courts continued to require procedural safeguards for people removed under the Alien Enemies Act.
